statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of five representative public templates/journeys. Authenticated edit, account, discussion submission and board.namu.wiki flows were not covered because they require separate permissions and/or represent another host.

paths.description: Entry page and wiki landing template; audited for navigation, consent, preferences, metadata, performance, privacy and accessibility.
Long-form article archetype represented by 대한민국; audited for long content, responsive layout, reading, crawler visibility and memory during repeated scrolling.
Live listing archetype represented by RecentChanges; audited for dense navigation and continuously changing content.
Primary search journey represented by a 대한민국 query; audited for end-to-end task completion, result state and form semantics.
Missing-document recovery state; audited for useful error messaging and recovery action.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the core page on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full modal covering the article before interaction; mobile leaves almost no content visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not gate reading behind the consent UI. Use a compact, non-modal notice for optional advertising choices and preserve immediate access to content.

findings.summary: Consent overlays use custom role=dialog containers rather than native dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The DOM recon found four DIV role=dialog surfaces and no native <dialog>; several hidden preference/vendor surfaces also add duplicate headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> only when modality is essential, with a labelled heading, focus management, Escape/cancel behavior and a clearly exposed decline action.

findings.summary: Page and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS on the home template, despite full-document wiki navigation being the dominant interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article, search and listing navigation, and disable non-essential motion under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long articles provide jump controls but no scroll-state-aware progress or responsive chrome.
findings.evidence: The article is about 25,101 CSS px tall; platform inspection found no scroll timeline or scroll-state styles, while screenshots show only fixed up/down controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative reading-progress indicator or scroll-state-aware header for long documents, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The layout adapts to mobile, but reusable components rely on viewport-level behavior rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: Both mobile layouts avoid horizontal overflow, but the platform probe found no @container rules on the template.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for article cards, tables and navigation modules that can appear in different content widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target support are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focused search input computed to outline:none and box-shadow:none; the UI probe found multiple links only 12–17 px high, and axe reported positive tabindex on search.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a strong outline, remove tabindex=1, and provide at least 24×24 CSS px targets with spacing, preferably 44×44 for primary mobile controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is outside the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 5.73 s, FCP 4.98 s and performance 65; the independent trace measured LCP 2.29 s, showing substantial condition-dependent delay.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the real LCP content, remove the initial redirect, and defer consent/ad code so core wiki content paints independently.

findings.summary: Startup includes avoidable long main-thread tasks.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 135 ms and TBT 113.7 ms; the long article mobile layout observed a 165 ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Split initialization work, defer advertising and consent scripts, and schedule non-critical tasks after content becomes interactive.

findings.summary: Redirects, blocking styles and an un-deferred ad script delay content delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded two redirects and 1.57 MB transferred; DOM confirmation shows adsbygoogle.js in HEAD with async=false/defer=false. Lighthouse estimates 1.51 s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the canonical home document directly, mark non-critical third-party scripts async/defer, and reduce or inline only truly critical CSS.

findings.summary: The page ships large amounts of unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 663 KiB unused JavaScript and 108 KiB unused CSS; HAR shows scripts account for 1.21 MB of transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split wiki features by route, remove duplicate ad/consent payloads, and load editor or account code only when requested.

findings.summary: Important links and images lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: axe reported critical image-alt failures and serious link-name failures; the images probe counted 14 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon links discernible names and give meaningful images alt text; mark purely decorative placeholders alt="" or role=presentation.

findings.summary: Text links fail minimum contrast and often rely on colour alone.
findings.evidence: axe found green text at 4.46:1 against #1c1d1f and orange links with only 1.66:1 contrast against surrounding text and no non-colour affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust dark-theme link colours to pass WCAG AA and underline body links or provide another persistent non-colour cue.

findings.summary: Landmarks and focus order are not robust.
findings.evidence: axe found content outside landmarks, tabindex=1, and unnamed links; the DOM has no main, nav or header elements and the focus probe showed no visible input outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce semantic header/nav/main landmarks, preserve DOM reading order, remove positive tabindex and style visible keyboard focus.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: The rendered meta viewport is user-scalable=no; axe classifies this as critical even though 360 px layouts do not horizontally overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and avoid restrictive maximum-scale values. Verify article tables and controls at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Most images omit intrinsic dimensions and several are oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 25 of 26 images missing a width or height attribute and 14 oversized; mobile layout recorded CLS around 0.05.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and choose source dimensions close to the rendered slot.

findings.summary: Loaded scripts trigger deprecated browser API warnings and large first-party bundles lack source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecations from the Cloudflare challenge script and failed valid-source-maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or configure third-party challenge code to avoid deprecated APIs and publish production source maps with controlled access.

findings.summary: Pages have descriptive titles but no standard meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM and discoverability evidence found no meta[name=description], and Lighthouse failed the meta-description audit; og:description exists only as social metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, page-specific meta description for home, article, listing and search templates.

findings.summary: The site exposes no sitemap at the conventional URL.
findings.evidence: robots.txt allows public wiki routes, but /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404. Canonical and successful page status were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index or document the supported sitemap location, and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Article pages provide Open Graph metadata but no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found complete og:* tags and zero JSON-LD blocks on an article-like page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Article/WebPage and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD derived from visible title, revision and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP is absent and one long-lived consent cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS and nosniff, but no CSP. Cookie audit found FCCDCF without Secure or HttpOnly, SameSite=None, expiring in about 390 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP and ensure every cross-site cookie that requires SameSite=None is Secure; minimise consent-cookie lifetime and scope.

findings.summary: The default page has a large advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 26 requests and 805,184 bytes to third parties; trackers found DoubleClick and Google syndication, while the consent copy names 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors to those necessary, block optional trackers until an affirmative choice, and batch/minimise measurement requests.

findings.summary: Several defensive browser policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, but omit CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and migrate clickjacking/XSS protection into a tested CSP with frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: The app-like wiki advertises mobile capability but has no manifest or active service worker controller.
findings.evidence: DOM recon found no manifest, while the UI probe reports service-worker support but controlled=false and metadata declares mobile-web-app-capable=yes.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intended, add a web app manifest and a minimal offline document fallback; otherwise remove misleading app-capable metadata.

findings.summary: Substantial non-Korean interface text is not language-scoped.
findings.evidence: The root correctly declares lang=ko, but the English consent dialog and Spanish/Portuguese footer are inside the same language context without nested lang attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lang attributes to foreign-language UI regions and localise consent/footer content consistently for the active locale.

findings.summary: The first consent surface emphasises acceptance and hides refusal behind settings.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show equally prominent Consent and Manage options buttons but no direct Reject all action, while copy requests personalised ads and sharing with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose Reject all beside Consent with equal prominence and make optional purposes off by default; keep the article usable regardless of choice.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and omits sizing metadata.
findings.evidence: Images probe found 14 oversized assets, 25 missing at least one intrinsic dimension, 12 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and two legacy PNGs.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized AVIF/WebP/SVG assets, preserve intrinsic dimensions and lazy-load below-fold content.

findings.summary: Advertising and consent work dominates a text-first page load.
findings.evidence: Scripts account for 1.21 MB; third parties account for 805 KB, and startup includes long tasks while the primary content is simple text.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize ad auctions or full vendor preference payloads until needed; schedule and cache background work at low priority.

findings.summary: Third-party transfer is disproportionate to the core wiki experience.
findings.evidence: More than half of 1.57 MB transferred is third-party, with ad and consent scripts among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors and defer all remaining non-essential scripts beyond core content.

findings.summary: The page is crawlable and responsive but not mobile-friendly for users who need zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse passes crawlable links and robots, while the viewport disables scaling with user-scalable=no.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep width=device-width but remove user-scalable=no so mobile users and accessibility tools can zoom.

taskList.title: Restore mobile zoom and test 200%/400% reflow.
Replace the reading-blocking consent wall with equal accept/reject controls and immediate content access.
Repair names, landmarks, target sizes, tab order and visible keyboard focus.
Fix dark-theme contrast and add non-colour link affordances.
Cut ad/consent startup cost, defer third parties, split unused code and prioritise core content.
Deploy CSP, secure cookies, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
Size, right-size and lazily deliver images.
Use native dialog semantics only where modality is essential.
Add meta descriptions, structured article data and a sitemap.
Language-scope or localise English, Spanish and Portuguese interface regions.
Remove deprecated API usage and publish controlled source maps.
Align mobile-app metadata with a manifest and offline fallback, or remove the claim.
Adopt container queries for reusable content modules.
Add declarative reading progress to very long articles.
Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with View Transitions.
